name: Lamech
charge: Killing a man and boasting of it; claiming seventy-sevenfold vengeance
summary: Cain's descendant Lamech, first recorded polygamist, told his two wives he had killed a man for wounding him and a young man for bruising him, and claimed that if Cain were avenged sevenfold, Lamech would be seventy-sevenfold.
offense: A killing far out of proportion to the injury, then a song to celebrate it. Lamech takes the protection God extended to Cain and twists it into a license for private vengeance without limit.
judgment: Scripture records no sentence on Lamech. His line is not heard from after the Flood account opens; the whole world of Cain's descendants ends in Genesis 7.

lawsResolved.text: Avenge not yourselves, for vengeance is in God's hands.
All boasting and bragging is wicked.
The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

text.text: And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.
Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
